summary.headline: Bansal Wire posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,308 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 105 crore, with EBITDA/ton near Rs 8,000 aided partly by inventory gain.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a record quarter for revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EBITDA per ton, recovering from a Q1 hit from industrial gas disruption and higher input costs. Sales volume was about 1,29,000 tons versus 1,14,609 tons in Q2 FY26, and operating cash flow was Rs 218 crore in the quarter and Rs 339 crore in H1. Management said about Rs 200/ton of EBITDA was a one-time inventory gain and guided to Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2. Raw material (wire rod) shortages hit October output, which management said is a short-term issue.

segments.name: IHT / OHT specialty wire
segments.commentary: IHT wire reached positive EBITDA last quarter; management cites Rs 15,000-20,000/ton EBITDA for the specialty wire group. IHT capacity is 9,000 tons, with 6,000 tons OHT being installed to reach 15,000 tons in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Steel tyre cord
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 20,000 tons, with a goal of 2 lakh tons. Pricing is about Rs 130-140/kg. First trial order received in Q2, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days; commercialisation possible within this year.

segments.name: Bead wire
segments.commentary: Nameplate capacity about 30,000 tons, with 10,000-15,000 tons currently run annually. Management cites Rs 12,000-15,000/ton EBITDA. Approvals not yet started; focus to resume in one to two quarters.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Less than 1% of sales. Management said it earns modest margins (about Rs 5,000-8,000/ton typical) due to industry overcapacity.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry)
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of Q2 volumes; management says B2C EBITDA is at least 50% higher than B2B.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% YoY for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 vs prior-year H2); management said Q1 losses cannot be recovered.
EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 FY27; management said Rs 7,000-8,000/ton is achievable for FY27 barring major geopolitical change.
Operating cash flow target of about Rs 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 combined; about Rs 350 crore already generated in H1 FY27.
Capacity to rise from 6.8 lakh tons to about 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year (60,000 tons Dadri brownfield plus about 90,000 tons Sanand greenfield).
Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore (also cited as Rs 200-250 crore per year), funded from internal accruals.
Long-term EBITDA/ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000, and above Rs 10,000 as specialty wire scales.
capex_capacity: Dadri: 60,000 tons additional low and high carbon wire capacity, mostly built; capitalisation expected by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27. Also 6,000 tons OHT wire, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Sanand (southern Gujarat) greenfield: about 90,000 tons of stainless steel and low carbon wire, with about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land (land acquired about a year ago). Some capitalisation expected from next quarter or the quarter after.
Steel tyre cord: 20,000 tons current capacity, with a 2 lakh ton goal; a bigger capex will follow customer approvals.
Management expects 4-5x asset turnover on new capacity.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering. Constraint is raw material supply rather than demand.
Wire rod shortage over the last 1.5-2 months as suppliers shifted output to TMT. Company holds about 1.5 months of inventory; October output was hit at some plants, which management says is now back.
Low carbon was about 55% of volume in Q2 (lower end of 55-60% target), supporting blended margin.
Gas prices are about 2.5x the regular level, passed through to customers. Availability has been stable for about one quarter.

Steel tyre cord India demand is 2.5-3 lakh tons, mostly imported. Management expects radialisation (about 60% in India truck/bus) to drive growth. Management says there is no Indian domestic competitor; Bekaert is the main competitor.
Management says it will cap any single customer at 20-25% of total sales for steel cord.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel tyre cord and IHT/OHT translate into revenue and EBITDA, and what is the EBITDA per ton for specialty wire?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel tyre cord is in trials, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days and commercialisation possible within the year. Specialty wire EBITDA is about Rs 15,000-20,000/ton, and IHT has turned EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA/ton came from inventory gains, and is Rs 7,000-7,500 conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about Rs 200/ton, so underlying EBITDA was about Rs 7,800-7,900/ton. Management said its own strategy is Rs 7,000-7,500 and it is not guiding above that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% volume growth guidance for H2 only, and is it at risk from raw material shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: It applies to H2 FY27, meaning Q3 and Q4 volumes up 20% YoY. Management said raw material shortages are temporary and that lost days can be made up the following month.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Sanand and Dadri CWIP and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is Rs 177 crore, mostly Dadri 60,000 tons. Sanand needs about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land.

qa_highlights.question: Steel cord capacity plan and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is 20,000 tons, the target is 2 lakh tons, and realisation is about Rs 130-140/kg. Management said a major capex will follow customer approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 7-7.5/kg the right base for H2 earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 7,000-7,500/ton is the H2 EBITDA commitment, and a better outcome is possible but not guided.

risks_watch: Raw material (wire rod) availability: shortages in October and supplier breakdowns could cut Q3 and Q4 volumes below the 20% growth guidance.
Gas prices at about 2.5x normal; management says pass-through to customers is in place, but this is a margin risk.
Q2 EBITDA/ton includes about Rs 200/ton inventory gain, so sustainability of the Rs 7,800-8,000 level is uncertain.
Steel cord commercialisation depends on customer approvals; management expects the first two quarters of ramp-up to be slow.
Sanand greenfield and Dadri ramp-up execution; capex may move beyond the stated timelines.
LRPC is loss-making at the margin due to industry overcapacity; management says it is less than 1% of sales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on results and guidance, with management saying it prefers to guide conservatively. It was candid about near-term raw material disruption and the Q1 gas hit. Answers on steel cord timelines were more hedged, using phrases such as "hopefully" and "if everything goes well".
key_quotes: We have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax.
So, we will rather be a little conservative than not delivering on our guidance.
Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500.
In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000.
